GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Buton Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as the organizer of Regional Government in the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Autonomous Region.

3. Regent is the Regent of Buton as the element who leads
4. Regional Apparatus is the supporting element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as PPPA Office is the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Buton Regency.

6. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD-PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems.
7. Forum for the Protection of Violence Victims, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.
8. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
9. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 years, including a child in the womb.
10. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
11. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
12. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
13. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child.
14. Companion is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
15. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
18. Violence against women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.

19. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the area of Buton Regency.
21. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
22. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
23. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
24. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer the case to the competent district court in matters and in the manner regulated in the law with a request to be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
25. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to act according to law against a person who has harmed him civilly.
26. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
27. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
28. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a regency that has a Child Rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

29. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Buton Regency.

Article 1l

Other violence as referred to in Article 5 letter f is caused by:
a. threat of violence, including any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, including a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 32

1. The Regional Government and the community are obliged to fulfill the rights of child victims of violence. (2) Forms of fulfillment of the rights of child victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (l) shall include fulfillment of the basic rights of children according to their needs.

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BUTON REGENCY

NUMBER 6 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER VIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 38

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence in the region.
2. Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
3. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers aspects related to planning and implementation.

(4) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers aspects related to planning, implementation, procedures, financing, quality, control and supervision.

5. Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted in accordance with laws and regulations.
6. Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted periodically.

CHAPTER X

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 40

1. The community participates in the organization of protection for Victims.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the sub-district/village level by the community;
b. establishing women and children protection units within community organizations;

18­
c. conducting socialization of women's and children's rights independently;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

CHAPTER VII

INFORMATION/REPORTING SYSTEM

Article 37

(1) The Regent implements an information/reporting system for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) The information/reporting system as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be organized in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 10

Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits whether material or immaterial; and/or
c. any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

CHAPTER IX

FINANCING

Article 39

The costs of implementing the organization of protection for children and women victims of violence, as well as the implementation of CFC development policies shall be charged to:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and/or
b. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 9

Neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is caused by:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of the child properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after the child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
c. acts that neglect a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
d. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Article 25

{1) Legal aid services as referred to in Article 20 letter e constitute services provided to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.

2. Services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of: a. legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. assistance to victims at the investigation, prosecution and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to fully describe the violence they have experienced,c. coordination with fellow law enforcers, volunteer assistants, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should; andd. reporting on case developments.

Article 6

Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

a. threat of violence, including any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

NUMBER 6 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

Article 26

1. Victim repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in Article 20 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment.
2. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (l) shall be carried out after the implementation of socialization related to the rights of women as victims.
3. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (I) shall be carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:a. the Provincial Regional Government;
b. other Regional Governments; andc. related government and non-government agencies and institutions.

CHAPTER VIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 38

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence in the region.
2. Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
3. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers aspects related to planning and implementation.

(4) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers aspects related to planning, implementation, procedures, financing, quality, control and supervision.

5. Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted in accordance with laws and regulations.
6. Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted periodically.

Article 1

In this Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Buton Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as the organizer of Regional Government in the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Autonomous Region.

7. Forum for the Protection of Violence Victims, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.
8. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
9. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 years, including a child in the womb.
10. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
11. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
12. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
13. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child.
14. Companion is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
15. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
18. Violence against women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.

19. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.

21. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
22. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
23. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
24. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer the case to the competent district court in matters and in the manner regulated in the law with a request to be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
25. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to act according to law against a person who has harmed him civilly.
26. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
27. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
28. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a regency that has a Child Rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

29. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Buton Regency.

Article 9

Neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is caused by:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of the child properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after the child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
c. acts that neglect a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
d. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

NUMBER 6 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BUTON REGENCY

NUMBER 6 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER VIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 38

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence in the region.
2. Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
3. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers aspects related to planning and implementation.

(4) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers aspects related to planning, implementation, procedures, financing, quality, control and supervision.

5. Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted in accordance with laws and regulations.
6. Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted periodically.

(2) Implementation of services to victims by UPTD-PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) may be delegated to other service units on a network basis.  (3) In carrying out services to victims as referred to in paragraph (1), UPTD-PPA is under and responsible to the Head of the PPPA Office and must coordinate with related fields.

(4] Further provisions regarding the establishment and working procedures of UPTD-PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

NUMBER 6 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to citizens in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services so minimum services for victims of violence are needed.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence, especially in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence.

Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a regency that has a Child Rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

29. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Buton Regency.

CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Part One

Regional Government

Article 26

1. Victim repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in Article 20 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment.
2. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (l) shall be carried out after the implementation of socialization related to the rights of women as victims.
3. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (I) shall be carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:a. the Provincial Regional Government;
b. other Regional Governments; andc. related government and non-government agencies and institutions.

CHAPTER VIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 38

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence in the region.
2. Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
3. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers aspects related to planning and implementation.

(4) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers aspects related to planning, implementation, procedures, financing, quality, control and supervision.

5. Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted in accordance with laws and regulations.
6. Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted periodically.

Article 31

Capital assistance as referred to in Article 28 letter c, shall include:
a. facilities and infrastructure assistance; andb. facilitation of working capital assistance.

Part Two

Community and Family

Article 19

1. In order to organize integrated services for Victims, the Regional Government establishes UPTD-PPA.  (2) Implementation of services to victims by UPTD-PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) may be delegated to other service units on a network basis.  (3) In carrying out services to victims as referred to in paragraph (1), UPTD-PPA is under and responsible to the Head of the PPPA Office and must coordinate with related fields.

(4] Further provisions regarding the establishment and working procedures of UPTD-PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Part Two

Integrated Services for Victims

Article 36

(1) In an effort to provide and organize service handling for victims, the Regional Government may establish FPKK.

2. FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to:
a. coordinate and synchronize service handling of UPTD-PPA;
b. maintain and develop networks and referral systems; and
c. collect, compile and present reports on violence.
3. The management and membership of FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be determined by Regent's Decree.
4. The membership of FPKK as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be grouped into the following roles:
a. health role;
b. psychology role;
c. legal role;
d. social role; and
e. economic role.
5. Further provisions regarding the establishment, main duties, and functions as well as membership of FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.
